neighbours.label: Malaysia and the Malay world: Malaysian cities and states (Penang, Kuala Lumpur, Sabah, Malacca), Borneo, the Malay language, and Singapore; Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines stay low
fire: Hawkers in Ipoh sell white coffee from tiny roadside stalls.
The old trading port of Malacca still has Dutch and Portuguese buildings.
Rangers in Sarawak counted orangutan nests along the river.
In the evening, crowds fill the night markets of Johor Bahru.
Many shop signs in Kota Kinabalu are written in Malay.
Commuters from Singapore cross the causeway every morning.
The rubber estates of Selangor were planted a century ago.
Fishing boats return to Kuala Terengganu before the monsoon.
quiet: Hawkers in Chiang Mai sell iced tea from tiny roadside stalls.
The old trading port of Hoi An still has Japanese and Chinese buildings.
Rangers in Sumatra counted tiger tracks along the river.
In the evening, crowds fill the night markets of Hanoi.
Many shop signs in Cebu are written in Tagalog.
Commuters from Hong Kong cross the border every morning.
The rubber estates of southern Thailand were planted a century ago.
Fishing boats return to Da Nang before the typhoon.
